messages.text: Write an email to a supplier about a late delivery.

Subject: Delayed Delivery

Dear [Supplier Name],

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to inquire about the status of our recent order, which has not yet arrived…

slides.note: Polite. Vague. Not ready to send.

slides.title:
Give it 4 things:
**who, what, tone, length.**

cards.title: The 4-part email
cards.text: Write an email to [WHO + HOW YOU KNOW THEM]. What: [WHAT HAPPENED + WHAT YOU NEED]. Tone: [E.G. FRIENDLY BUT FIRM]. Length: under [N] words.

messages.text: Write an email to Dan, our regular flour supplier. What: Tuesday's order hasn't arrived, I need it by Friday morning or I'll buy elsewhere this week. Tone: friendly but firm. Under 60 words.

Hi Dan,

Tuesday's flour order still hasn't arrived. Could you check where it is? I need it by Friday morning at the latest, otherwise I'll have to buy elsewhere this week.

Can you let me know today?

Thanks,
[YOUR NAME]

slides.title: Length is the one people skip.
paras: Add **"under 60 words"** and the waffle goes.

caption:
How to write better emails with AI: who, what, tone, length

"Write an email to a supplier about a late delivery" gets you "I hope this email finds you well" and a [Supplier Name] blank. Polite, vague, not ready to send.

Give it 4 things instead:

"Write an email to [WHO + HOW YOU KNOW THEM]. What: [WHAT HAPPENED + WHAT YOU NEED]. Tone: [E.G. FRIENDLY BUT FIRM]. Length: under [N] words."

I filled it in for an example bakery chasing a late flour order and got 5 short lines: what's missing, the Friday deadline, what happens if not, and a clear ask. Ready to send after a quick read.

Tip: length is the one people skip. A word limit cuts the waffle.
